numeric_mode_note: Public translation is Pythonic. Exact REAL restrictions below preserve the legacy contract for a future strict milestone; see ../numeric-modes.md.
python_reference_checked: 2026-10-13; Python 3.11.17 documentation, not execution on controller Python 3.11.5
boundary: Documented DELAY source/range rules with tested calling-host-thread blocking and injected-sleeper behavior. No controller scheduling, motion, pause, abort, RMI timing or runtime equivalence is established.

rules.documented: The argument is an INTEGER expression specifying milliseconds. Zero has no effect. A value below zero or greater than one day causes an execution error.
rules.implemented: DELAY expression is checked as INTEGER and evaluated once. Runtime accepts 0..86400000 milliseconds inclusive and rejects invalid values before calling the host sleeper. BYTE/SHORT values use existing checked INTEGER promotion. Uninitialized/unknown reads and integer-expression errors keep their existing guards.
rules.restriction: Range failures use source-located KarelRuntimeError rather than authenticated FANUC alarm/task state. The step budget counts statements and does not impose a wall-clock timeout. %DELAY, PAUSE, ABORT and condition handlers remain blocked.

rules.feature: Host sleeping and injectable test adapter
rules.python_pdf: B-84464EN-26_01_01.pdf PDF pages 18-19, I.4.3: time is listed among tested standard-library modules
rules.implemented: Program(sleep=None) uses Python time.sleep(milliseconds / 1000.0). Program(sleep=callable) binds a per-instance synchronous callback accepting seconds and returning None. Zero skips the callback, avoiding the host-thread yield of time.sleep(0). Calls block ordinary generated execution until the callback returns. Tests inject recorders; the small runnable example uses only seven milliseconds of requested default host sleep.
rules.restriction: Host seconds conversion is adapter arithmetic and does not widen the exact KAREL REAL subset. Python sleep may last longer because of host scheduling, while KAREL documents rounding/$SCR.$cond_time behavior. None of motion continuation, controller pause/resume timing, abort cancellation, task holds or RMI queue semantics is modeled. Injected callbacks are explicitly supplied Python behavior, not controller clock models.

rules.feature: Routine timing effects and failure cleanup
rules.implemented: Reports identify source DELAY statements and propagate potential_host_delays through routine call graphs, including recursive paths. May-delay function calls retain conservative operator/indexed-target ordering guards. Defined single-expression duration calls are evaluated once. Prior writes persist on runtime range/sleeper errors and routine frames unwind. Ordinary callback exceptions become source-located KarelRuntimeError with chained causes; KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit propagate through cleanup.
rules.restriction: Potential timing effects are conservative and include statically present DELAY statements even when skipped or zero. Callback return values other than None are rejected. Existing scalar/reference, argument-order, FOR-counter and control-flow restrictions are unchanged.
rules.tests: tests/test_delays.py: call graph, recursive, control-flow, ordering and error tests

abort_update.boundary: Bare ABORT terminates this offline instance without rollback; no task/action/condition or motion semantics. Routine effects propagate and frames unwind; direct FOR use requires fresh routine-local counters.
